title: The ideal of a complete ring lies in the Jacobson radical
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Then $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$: $1+x$ is a unit for every $x\in I$, equivalently every maximal ideal of $A$ contains $I$. Consequently every nonempty closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ meets $V(I)$ (it is $V(J)$ for an ideal $J\ne A$, and a maximal ideal containing $J$ contains $I$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 05GI (label lemma-radical-completion), part (4), applied to A = A^wedge; the last sentence is the definition of the Zariski topology together with the existence of maximal ideals over a proper ideal
